([[Hyattsville, Maryland]]) | college = * [[UAB Blazers men's basketball|UAB]] (2016–2018) * [[Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens men's basketball|Delaware]] (2019–2020) | draft_year = 2020 | career_start = 2020 | years1 = {{nbay|2020|full=y}} | team1 = [[Charlotte Hornets]] | years2 = [[2020–21 NBA G League season|2021]] | team2 = →[[Greensboro Swarm]] | years3 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021]]–[[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]] | team3 = [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|Agua Caliente / Ontario / San Diego Clippers]] | years4 = 2025–2026 | team4 = [[Élan Chalon]] | years5 = 2026–present | team5 = [[Bilbao Basket]] | highlights = * First-team All-[[Colonial Athletic Association|CAA]] (2020) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport | Men's basketball}} {{MedalCountry|{{flagu|Canada}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Under-19 World Cup]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2017 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2017 Egypt]]|[[Canada men's national basketball team|National team]]}} {{MedalCompetition| [[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|FIBA Americas U18 Championship]]| [[Canada men's national under-19 basketball team|National team]]}} {{MedalSilver| [[2016 FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|2016 Chile]] | [[Canada men's national under-19 basketball team|National team]]}} }} '''Nathan Joseph Darling''' (born August 30, 1998) is a Canadian professional [[basketball]] player for [[Bilbao Basket]] of the [[Liga ACB]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UAB Blazers men's basketball|UAB Blazers]] and the [[Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens men's basketball|Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens]]. He is the first and only Blue Hens player in [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] history.{{cite web|title=Delaware Players in the NBA|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/ncaa/conferences/Colonial-Athletic-Association/15/Delaware/116/nba-players|website=RealGM.com|access-date=February 7, 2022}} ==High school career== Darling attended [[DeMatha Catholic High School]] and was teammates with top recruit [[Markelle Fultz]] and football star [[Chase Young]].{{cite news |last1=Tresolini |first1=Kevin |title=Former DeMatha guard Darling transfers to Delaware from UAB |url=https://www.delawareonline.com/story/sports/college/2018/04/25/former-dematha-guard-darling-transfers-delaware-uab/550885002/ |accessdate=April 9, 2020 |work=The News Journal |date=April 25, 2018}} ==College career== Darling began his collegiate career at [[UAB Blazers men's basketball|UAB]] and averaged 2.5 points per game. As a sophomore, he averaged 10.1 points per game while shooting 40.9 percent on three-pointers. Following the season, he decided to transfer to the [[University of Delaware]]. On December 14, 2019, Darling scored a game-high 29 points against 20th-ranked [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]] in a 78–70 loss, after which his head coach [[Martin Ingelsby]] said he was playing like one of the best guards in college basketball.{{cite news |title=Bedford's Nate Darling declares for NBA draft |url=https://www.thechronicleherald.ca/sports/local-sports/bedfords-nate-darling-declares-for-nba-draft-435312/ |accessdate=April 9, 2020 |work=[[The Chronicle Herald]] |date=April 8, 2020}} As a junior, Darling averaged 21 points per game.{{cite web |title=Nate Darling Enters 2020 NBA Draft Process, Maintains Eligibility |url=https://bluehens.com/news/2020/4/7/mens-basketball-nate-darling-enters-2020-nba-draft-process-maintains-eligibility.aspx |website=[[Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens]] |accessdate=April 9, 2020 |date=April 7, 2020}} He earned first-team All-[[Colonial Athletic Association]] (CAA) honors.{{cite press release|url=https://caasports.com/news/2020/3/4/caa-announces-mens-basketball-postseason-accolades.aspx |title=CAA Basketball Announces Men's Basketball Postseason Accolades |publisher=Colonial Athletic Association |date=March 6, 2020 |accessdate=March 6, 2020}} After the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] while retaining college eligibility.{{cite news |last1=Daly |first1=Brian |title=Bedford's Nate Darling declares for NBA draft, retains college eligibility |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/nova-scotia/nova-scotia-nate-darling-declares-for-nba-draft-retains-college-eligibility-1.5525187 |accessdate=April 8, 2020 |work=CBC |date=April 7, 2020}} However, on August 3 he announced he was remaining in the draft and turning professional.{{cite news |title=Bedford's Nate Darling goes all in on NBA Draft hopes |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/nova-scotia/nba-draft-nate-darling-2020-1.5672875 |accessdate=August 3, 2020 |work=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]] |date=August 3, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Charlotte Hornets (2020–2021)=== After going undrafted in the [[2020 NBA draft]], Darling signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Charlotte Hornets]]. Under the terms of the deal, he will split time between the Hornets and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Greensboro Swarm]].{{cite news |last1=Palmeter |first1=Paul |title=Nate Darling goes undrafted but will sign deal with NBA club |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/nova-scotia/nate-darling-nba-draft-club-team-charlotte-hornets-1.5807829 |accessdate=November 19, 2020 |work=[[CBC News]] |date=November 19, 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/charlotte-hornets-sign-grant-riller-nate-darling|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign Grant Riller and Nate Darling to Two-Way Contracts|date=November 30, 2020|work=NBA.com|accessdate=December 14, 2020}} This united him with Canadian assistant coach [[Jay Triano]]. He made his NBA debut on March 13, 2021, against the [[Toronto Raptors]], hitting a three-pointer in the fourth quarter, and became the first Nova Scotia born player in NBA history.{{cite web |last1=Rafferty |first1=Scott |title=Nova Scotia native and Charlotte Hornets guard Nate Darling scores first NBA basket |url=https://ca.nba.com/news/nova-scotia-native-and-charlotte-hornets-guard-nate-darling-scores-first-nba-basket/1tl2pfedwj6v71b66q7zmaaxxc |website=NBA.com |access-date=October 17, 2021 |date=March 25, 2021}} ===Agua Caliente / Ontario / San Diego Clippers (2021–present)=== On October 16, 2021, Darling was signed by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], but was waived shortly thereafter.{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Clippers Sign, Waive Nate Darling|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/10/clippers-sign-waive-nate-darling.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 16, 2021|access-date=October 17, 2021}} On October 23, he was selected by the [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|Agua Caliente Clippers]] fifth overall in the [[2021 NBA G League draft (October)|2021 NBA G League draft]].{{cite web|title=2021 NBA G League Draft Board|url=https://gleague.nba.com/2021-nba-g-league-draft-order/|website=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} On February 17, 2023, Darling signed a two-way contract with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|first=Rory|last=Maher|title=Clippers Sign Nate Darling To Two-Way Deal|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/02/clippers-sign-nate-darling-to-two-way-deal.html|website=HoopsRumors.comdate=February 17, 2023|access-date=February 17, 2023}} He was waived four days later without having played a game for the NBA team.{{cite tweet|first=Andrew|last=Greif|title=The Clippers say they've waived Nate Darling, who was recently signed to a two-way deal.|number=1628156570562596867|user=AndrewGreif|date=February 21, 2023|access-date=February 21, 2023}} On February 23, he was reacquired by the [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|Ontario Clippers]].{{cite web|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/22-23-nba-g-league-transactions|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 23, 2023}} On October 9, 2023, Darling signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]],{{cite web|first=Dana|last=Gauruder|title=Clippers Waive Brodric Thomas, Sign Nate Darling|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/10/clippers-to-waive-thomas-sign-darling.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 9, 2023|access-date=October 11, 2023}} but was waived on October 20, prior to the start of the 2023–24 season.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Clippers Sign Joey Hauser, Cut Two Players|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/10/clippers-sign-joey-hauser-cut-two-players.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 20, 2023|access-date=October 22, 2023}} Ten days later, he rejoined the [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|Ontario Clippers]].{{cite web|title=Ontario Clippers Announce Training Camp Roster for 2023-24 NBA G League Season|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/09/clippers-to-sign-elijah-harkless-to-exhibit-10-contract.html|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=September 14, 2024}} On September 20, 2024, Darling signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], but was waived on October 12.{{cite web|first=Rory|last=Maher|title=Clippers Sign, Waive Nate Darling|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/clippers-to-sign-nate-darling-to-exhibit-10-deal.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 12, 2024|access-date=October 12, 2024}} On October 28, he rejoined the [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego Clippers]].{{cite web|title=SAN DIEGO CLIPPERS ANNOUNCE TRAINING CAMP ROSTER FOR 2024-25 NBA G LEAGUE SEASON|url=https://sandiego.gleague.nba.com/news/san-diego-clippers-announce-training-camp-roster-for-2024-25-nba-g-league-season|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 2, 2024}} On August 5, 2025, he signed with [[Elan Chalon]] of the French [[LNB Pro A]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.elanchalon.com/nate-darling-arrive-a-lelan-chalon/|title=Nate Darling arrive à l’Elan Chalon|last=|first=|date=August 5, 2025|website=elanchalon.com|publisher=|language=fr|access-date=September 1, 2025}} On June 19, 2026, he signed with [[Bilbao Basket]] of the [[Liga ACB]].{{Cite
